body:
I think that I also just ran into this bug with a `cc_binary` rule with `linkshared = True`.

I'm using

- macOS v11.0.1
- Bazel v3.7.0
- The latest `@rules_cc` commit, `b1c40e1`

At some moment minor problems with the built-in rules like this one started to cause us so much pain that we reimplemented most cc rules in Starlark. For compilation we use [cc_common.compile](https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/skylark/lib/cc_common.html#compile), but for linking we cannot use [cc_common.link](https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/skylark/lib/cc_common.html#link) because it brings back all the same problems, so linking is re-implemented all the way down to [actions.run](https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/skylark/lib/actions.html#run).
This is still an issue with `4.0.0`.

I ran into this with bazel 4.0.0, using `cc_binary` and `linkshared = True`

However, one quick fix seems to be to provide the full file name (with extension) as the name of the rule. So instead of using `name = "mylib"` which ends up generating `libmylib.so`, I use `name = "libmylib.dylib"` and it generates `libmylib.dylib`!

For my purposes this seem to work fine (I am doing something with JNI so I need the native libraries to have a very specific name with .dylib so that the JVM can load them properly).

I investigated this further and can say that it is *not* a problem with `cc_common.link`, but rather with the auto-configured Unix toolchain: It should set `artifact_name_patterns` in [`cc_common.create_cc_toolchain_config_info`](https://docs.bazel.build/versions/main/skylark/lib/cc_common.html#create_cc_toolchain_config_info), but doesn't. This can be worked around by specifying a custom toolchain.

issue.title: Use .dylib extension for macOS dynamic libraries in Unix toolchain

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
The autoconfigured Unix toolchain previously did not set any artifact_name_patterns, which meant that all artifacts used the default(Linux) patterns. This was incorrect in the case of dynamic libraries on macOS, which should have the extension `.dylib` rather than `.so`.

Fixes #11082.

body:
Yes, I confirm that providing the toolchain with the properly configured `artifact_name_patterns` fixes the issue. Thank you!
